title: Thirteen years in Chicago; New York in 1926 with Cliff Jackson
summary: He was never used by Jimmie Noone. He stayed 13 years in Chicago, but first went to New York in 1926 to play with Cliff Jackson at the Capitol Palace. New Yorkers did not understand New Orleans jazz.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Jimmy Newton was in Chicago at that time. Did you ever work with Jimmy Newton? No, I never worked with him. He never did use me. I don't know why. How long were you in Chicago?

Right. Well, just like I told you, I went there in 29. I stood there a while and traveled in and out. Then came back. All again, I stayed in Chicago for 13 years. Did you ever get to New York to do any musicians? Yeah. I played in New York before... I went to New York before I went to Chicago. I went to New York in 26. I was playing with Cliff Jackson and his crazy cats at the Capitol Palace on Lenox Avenue. What was the personnel of that band, do you recall? Well, it's kind of hard. I'd have to look it up, you know. Cliff Jackson?

He said, care for his society right now, I think. And were there many New Orleans jazz musicians in New York at that time? No, no, no. What did New York think of jazz on the whole, I mean, at that time? Were there many engagements for jazz bands there?

No, it looked like it was a different style altogether. Couldn't get them to understand Lewis. Just like Lewis, well, whatever he'd play there, he'd go over great. But most of the musicians up there, they was playing that Eastern style, fast music and jumble up.
